PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Love is a Christian value that God shows to children and that children are called to show to others. In this sub-strand you will read Matthew 19:13-15, see how Jesus received and blessed children, learn to show kindness, and thank God for His love by obeying His teachings.

## Strand 4.0: Christian Values
Sub-strand 4.4: Love
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) recognise that God loves children; Matthew 19:13-15
b) demonstrate love by showing kindness to others
c) appreciate God’s love by obeying His teachings

## Key inquiry questions
1. How did Jesus Christ show love to children?
2. How do you show Godly love to others as a Christian?

## Core competencies
• Imagination and Creativity: the skill of coming up with unique and new ideas is exhibited as learners draw Jesus praying for children.
• Digital Literacy: the skill of digital citizenship is portrayed as learners watch a video clip on Jesus Christ blessing children.

## Values
• Love: learners show love to others as taught by Jesus Christ.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Social cohesion: teamwork is portrayed as learners take up different roles in performing assigned tasks.

## Links to other learning areas
• English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the Holy Bible.
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners draw and role play.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 4.0 Christian Values, Sub-strand 4.4 Love
• Matthew 19:13-15

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Jesus receives the children

LESSON 1: JESUS RECEIVES THE CHILDREN
=====================================

## What you will learn
• Retell Matthew 19:13-15 in the correct order.
• Explain how Jesus showed that God loves children.

Curriculum outcomes: a) recognise that God loves children; Matthew 19:13-15

## Introduction
Some adults think children should keep quiet and stay out of the way. In Matthew 19:13-15, people brought children to Jesus, and the way he received them shows God's love for every child.

## Notes
### What Matthew 19:13-15 says
The passage is short. These are the events it records, in order.

- People brought little children to Jesus. They wanted him to put his hands on the children and pray for them.
- The disciples rebuked the people who brought the children. They tried to stop this from happening.
- Jesus did not agree with the disciples. He said, "Let the little children come to me, and do not forbid them, for of such is the kingdom of heaven."
- Jesus laid his hands on the children. Then he went on from there.

The older Bible word "suffer" in this verse means "allow". Jesus was telling the disciples to let the children come.

### How Jesus showed love
Jesus did not send the children away. He stopped those who were blocking them. He laid his hands on them and prayed, which is the blessing the people had asked for. Then he continued his journey. Children were not a nuisance to him. They were welcome.

"Of such is the kingdom of heaven" means that the kingdom of heaven belongs to people who come to God with a trusting heart, the kind of heart seen in a little child. God loves children and wants them near him.

### What we learn
- God loves children. Jesus Christ showed that love by receiving them.
- No child is too small to come to Jesus.
- Adults, including the disciples, can be wrong when they push children aside. Jesus corrected them.
- Placing his hands on the children and praying for them was an act of blessing and care.

Christians remember this story when they welcome children in church, at home and at school.

## Key words
• rebuke — to speak sharply to someone to stop them
• bless — to pray for God's goodness on a person; Jesus did this by laying his hands on the children
• kingdom of heaven — God's reign; Jesus said it belongs to people who are like these children

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A learner says, "The disciples were right to send the children away because Jesus was busy." What does Matthew 19:13-15 show?

Working:
1. The disciples did rebuke the people who brought the children.
2. Jesus told them to let the children come and not to forbid them.
3. He laid his hands on the children.

Answer: Jesus did not agree with the disciples. He welcomed the children and blessed them.

## Activity: Retell and role-play Matthew 19:13-15
You will need: Bible, Exercise book, Drawing paper and pencils
1. In groups, read Matthew 19:13-15 and retell Jesus Christ's love for children in the order of the passage.
2. Role-play Jesus blessing the children: one learner reads Jesus' words, others act as the people, the children and the disciples.
3. Draw Jesus praying for the children, showing him laying his hands on them.
4. If a video clip on Jesus Christ blessing children is available, watch it with the teacher and say which parts match Matthew 19:13-15.

## Practice
1. Why did people bring little children to Jesus in Matthew 19:13?
2. What did the disciples do, and what did Jesus say?
3. What did Jesus do before he went on from there?
4. How did Jesus show that God loves children?

## Summary
• People brought children so that Jesus would lay his hands on them and pray.
• Jesus refused to send the children away and said the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.
• God loves children, and Jesus showed that love by blessing them.

### Answers to practice
1. They wanted him to put his hands on the children and pray for them.
2. The disciples rebuked the people. Jesus said to let the little children come to him and not to forbid them, for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
3. He laid his hands on the children.
4. He welcomed them, told the disciples not to stop them, and laid his hands on them and prayed.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Showing kindness to others

LESSON 2: SHOWING KINDNESS TO OTHERS
====================================

## What you will learn
• Explain how kindness shows Christian love.
• Give examples of kindness at home, at school and in church.

Curriculum outcomes: b) demonstrate love by showing kindness to others

## Introduction
Jesus did not only say that children were welcome. He laid his hands on them and prayed. Love is shown in actions. Christians demonstrate love by showing kindness to others.

## Notes
### Kindness is love in action
To demonstrate love means to show it, not only to talk about it. Kindness is a way of showing love. A kind person looks for the good of another person and does something helpful.

Jesus showed this kind of love when he received the children. He corrected the disciples, made time for the children, and blessed them. Godly love follows that example. It is patient, fair and helpful. It does not embarrass people or help them only when others are watching.

### Kindness at school
- Share a pencil, an eraser or a seat with a learner who has none.
- Help a classmate who has fallen, or explain work the classmate did not understand.
- Invite a learner who is standing alone to join the game.
- Speak politely. Do not laugh at someone's mistake or clothes.
- Pick up litter in the classroom even if you did not drop it.

### Kindness at home and in the community
- Help with chores: washing utensils, sweeping, looking after a younger child.
- Speak gently to parents, guardians, brothers and sisters.
- Pray for a person who is sick and, if your family allows, visit with them.
- Forgive a person who says sorry.
- Give way to an older person and greet neighbours respectfully.

### Kindness that is not Godly love
A person may offer gifts to trick a child into a secret or a wrong act. That is not the love Jesus taught. Godly love never asks you to lie, to hide things from your parents, or to do what God forbids. True kindness wants what is good and stays inside God's teachings.

## Key words
• kindness — showing love by helpful, gentle actions
• demonstrate — to show something by what you do
• Godly love — love that follows the teaching and example of Jesus Christ

## Worked examples

### Example 1
During break, one learner has no pencil for the next lesson. Two classmates have extra pencils. What would showing Godly love look like?

Working:
1. Love is shown by kindness, as Jesus showed love by what he did for the children.
2. A spare pencil meets a real need.
3. The help should be given freely, without mocking the learner.

Answer: Lend or give a pencil kindly, so the learner can do the lesson.

## Activity: Show love as Jesus taught
You will need: Manila paper, Marker pens
1. In groups, list ways to show love to others as taught by Jesus Christ, at home, at school and in church.
2. Act one of the kind actions in a short play.
3. Each learner chooses one kind act to do before the next lesson and later tells the class what happened.

## Practice
1. How do Christians demonstrate love?
2. Give two ways of showing kindness at school.
3. Why is a gift that asks you to keep a bad secret not Godly love?

## Summary
• Love is shown by kind actions, as Jesus showed love to children.
• Kindness at home and at school includes sharing, helping, speaking politely and including others.
• Godly love never leads a person into wrong.

### Answers to practice
1. By showing kindness to others in what they do and say.
2. Any two, for example sharing a pencil, helping a classmate, including someone in a game, or speaking politely.
3. Godly love never asks a child to hide wrong things from parents or to disobey God.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Thanking God by obeying Him

LESSON 3: THANKING GOD BY OBEYING HIM
=====================================

## What you will learn
• Explain how obedience shows thanks for God's love.
• Name teachings of God that a Grade 4 learner can obey.

Curriculum outcomes: c) appreciate God’s love by obeying His teachings

## Introduction
When someone loves you and cares for you, a thankful child listens to that person. Christians appreciate God's love by obeying His teachings, not only by singing about love.

## Notes
### Love and obedience belong together
Matthew 19:13-15 shows that God loves children. Jesus made room for them and blessed them. Appreciating that love means valuing it and answering it. One clear answer is obedience. We do what God teaches because we are grateful, not because we are trying to earn his love. He already loves children.

If a person says "God loves me" and then keeps doing what God forbids, the words and the life do not match. Obedience is how thanks becomes visible.

### Teachings a learner can obey
- Love God and love other people. Kindness, sharing and forgiveness put love into practice.
- Honour your parents and guardians. Listen when they guide you and speak to them with respect.
- Tell the truth, even when the truth may bring a correction.
- Do not steal. Return what is not yours.
- Keep your body for what is right. Say no to sexual sin and to people who want you to do wrong.
- Do not bully, insult or fight.
- Pray, and treat the church as God's house.
- Welcome other children, remembering that Jesus welcomed children.

### A daily way to appreciate God's love
In the morning, thank God for his love and ask for help to obey. During the day, choose the kind and honest action. In the evening, think of one teaching you obeyed and one you need to obey better tomorrow. When you fail, tell God you are sorry and start again. That desire to obey is itself a way of appreciating his love.

## Key words
• appreciate — to value something and show that it matters to you
• obey — to do what God, a parent or a teacher has taught
• teaching — what God has told his people to believe and to do

## Activity: Obeying God's teachings
You will need: Bible, Exercise book
1. Read Matthew 19:13-15 again and say one way Jesus showed love.
2. In pairs, list God's teachings that a learner can obey at home and at school.
3. Each learner writes: "I appreciate God's love by..." and completes the sentence with one act of obedience.
4. Share two sentences with the class.

## Practice
1. How can a Christian appreciate God's love?
2. Give three teachings a Grade 4 learner can obey.
3. Why is obedience a better thanks than words alone?

## Summary
• God already loves children, as Jesus showed in Matthew 19:13-15.
• We appreciate that love by obeying his teachings.
• Truth, kindness, respect for parents and a pure life are ways of obeying.

### Answers to practice
1. By obeying God's teachings.
2. Any three, for example love others, honour parents, tell the truth, do not steal, keep the body pure, do not bully, and pray.
3. Obedience shows that God's love matters in daily actions, so the life matches the words.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 4.4 LOVE
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. According to Matthew 19:13, why were little children brought to Jesus?
   A. To be counted in a census
   B. So that he would lay his hands on them and pray
   C. To sing in the temple
   D. To carry his bag

2. What did the disciples do when the children were brought?
   A. They blessed the children
   B. They rebuked the people who brought them
   C. They left Jesus
   D. They gave the children food

3. Which words did Jesus speak about the children?
   A. Send them away until they are older
   B. Let the little children come to me, and do not forbid them
   C. Only boys may come
   D. Children must keep silent

4. What did Jesus do to the children before he departed?
   A. He sent them to buy food
   B. He laid his hands on them
   C. He told them to go back to Egypt
   D. He wrote their names

5. Which action demonstrates love by kindness?
   A. Laughing at a classmate's torn uniform
   B. Sharing your pencil with a learner who has none
   C. Hiding the class ball
   D. Pushing in the queue

6. A stranger offers sweets if you will keep a meeting secret from your parents. Is that Godly love?

7. How do Christians appreciate God's love?
   A. By ignoring his teachings
   B. By obeying his teachings
   C. By boasting about their gifts
   D. By staying away from church

8. Give two teachings of God that a learner can obey this week.

9. What does "of such is the kingdom of heaven" teach us about children?

10. Name one kind act at home and one kind act at school.
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 4.4 LOVE
========================================

1. B. So that he would lay his hands on them and pray
   The people wanted Jesus to put his hands on the children and pray.

2. B. They rebuked the people who brought them
   Matthew 19:13 says the disciples rebuked them.

3. B. Let the little children come to me, and do not forbid them
   Jesus told the disciples not to stop the children, for of such is the kingdom of heaven.

4. B. He laid his hands on them
   Matthew 19:15 says he laid his hands on them and departed.

5. B. Sharing your pencil with a learner who has none
   Sharing meets a need and shows Godly love in action.

6. No. Godly love does not ask a child to hide things from parents or to do wrong.
   Kindness that leads a child into secrecy and danger is not the love Jesus taught.

7. B. By obeying his teachings
   The learning outcome is to appreciate God's love by obeying his teachings.

8. Any two, for example tell the truth, honour parents, be kind, do not steal, and pray.
   Obedience is the way a child shows thanks for God's love.

9. God welcomes children. The kingdom of heaven belongs to people who come to him with a trusting heart like theirs.
   These are Jesus' words in Matthew 19:14.

10. Home: any helpful act such as chores or gentle speech. School: any helpful act such as sharing, including others or helping a classmate.
   Kindness in both places demonstrates Christian love.

2. In pairs, list God's teachings that a learner can obey at home and at school.
3. Each learner writes: "I appreciate God's love by..." and completes the sentence with one act of obedience.
4. Share two sentences with the class.

## Practice
1. How can a Christian appreciate God's love?
2. Give three teachings a Grade 4 learner can obey.
3. Why is obedience a better thanks than words alone?

## Summary
• God already loves children, as Jesus showed in Matthew 19:13-15.
• We appreciate that love by obeying his teachings.
• Truth, kindness, respect for parents and a pure life are ways of obeying.

### Answers to practice
1. By obeying God's teachings.
2. Any three, for example love others, honour parents, tell the truth, do not steal, keep the body pure, do not bully, and pray.
3. Obedience shows that God's love matters in daily actions, so the life matches the words.

questions.question: According to Matthew 19:13, why were little children brought to Jesus?
options: To be counted in a census
So that he would lay his hands on them and pray
questions.explanation: The people wanted Jesus to put his hands on the children and pray.

questions.question: What did the disciples do when the children were brought?
options: They rebuked the people who brought them
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:13 says the disciples rebuked them.

questions.question: Which words did Jesus speak about the children?
options: Send them away until they are older
Let the little children come to me, and do not forbid them
questions.explanation: Jesus told the disciples not to stop the children, for of such is the kingdom of heaven.

questions.question: What did Jesus do to the children before he departed?
options: He sent them to buy food
He laid his hands on them
He told them to go back to Egypt
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:15 says he laid his hands on them and departed.

questions.question: Which action demonstrates love by kindness?
options: Laughing at a classmate's torn uniform
Sharing your pencil with a learner who has none
questions.explanation: Sharing meets a need and shows Godly love in action.

questions.question: A stranger offers sweets if you will keep a meeting secret from your parents. Is that Godly love?
questions.answer: No. Godly love does not ask a child to hide things from parents or to do wrong.
questions.explanation: Kindness that leads a child into secrecy and danger is not the love Jesus taught.

questions.question: How do Christians appreciate God's love?
questions.explanation: The learning outcome is to appreciate God's love by obeying his teachings.

questions.question: Give two teachings of God that a learner can obey this week.
questions.answer: Any two, for example tell the truth, honour parents, be kind, do not steal, and pray.
questions.explanation: Obedience is the way a child shows thanks for God's love.

questions.question: What does "of such is the kingdom of heaven" teach us about children?
questions.answer: God welcomes children. The kingdom of heaven belongs to people who come to him with a trusting heart like theirs.
questions.explanation: These are Jesus' words in Matthew 19:14.

questions.question: Name one kind act at home and one kind act at school.
questions.answer: Home: any helpful act such as chores or gentle speech. School: any helpful act such as sharing, including others or helping a classmate.
questions.explanation: Kindness in both places demonstrates Christian love.
